entries.title: kb_export auto-commit is opt-in and defaults to off
entries.summary: bible.autoCommit in FLEET_DIR/knowledge/config.json defaults to FALSE. kb_import preserves a bible entry CONFIRMED confidence as its sole exemption from the confidence clamp, justified by the bible being a git-reviewed, human-merged artifact -- which auto-committing as pm-kb, mid-sprint, on a feature branch did not make true.

entries.title: Confidence decay only ever touched empty-basis entries, so it is now legacy-only
entries.summary: decayConceptEntries() matches only rows whose source_files is empty. Since capture refuses to create such a row, the INFERRED -> UNVERIFIED ladder can fire only on rows predating that gate. Staleness for basis-carrying entries is freshnessSweep's job, which flags stale rather than downgrading confidence -- the two are not substitutes.

entries.title: Role agents decide KB work; the engine executes it
entries.summary: doer, reviewer, planner and harvester return kb_captures in their structured output, and the reviewer alone returns kb_promotions -- widening capture does not widen promotion. The engine validates the payload and drops anything a downstream tool would refuse, so a bad payload never becomes a call. fleet-sprint makes the calls directly through its injected callTool; apra-pm auto-sprint cannot, because Claude workflow scripts have no tool access, so it dispatches one cheap executor agent instead.

entries.title: The provider carries the repo its KB is about
entries.summary: SqliteProvider takes a repoPath, threaded from createKbProvidersForSlug, and resolves relative source_files against it at capture, at promote and at prime-time freshness. Without it those paths resolve against the fleet server process cwd, which is the apra-fleet-tm7 repo-blindness defect. The shared global KB deliberately has no repoPath: it spans every repo, so it enforces the empty-basis rule only.

entries.title: kb_list reads through SqliteProvider.list(), which bumps no telemetry
entries.summary: kb_list is a read-only audit path using a dedicated list() method rather than query(), so it issues a pure SELECT without incrementing use_count or last_accessed. Its projection deliberately omits tags -- use kb_query to inspect them.

entries.title: The bible is a v2 envelope recording its export commit
entries.summary: kb_export writes {version:2, provenance:{commit, branch, entry_count}, entries}. A commit is recorded rather than a timestamp because entries are id-sorted so re-exports produce meaningful diffs, and a timestamp would produce a diff on every export. kb_import accepts BOTH the v2 object and a legacy bare array, selecting on Array.isArray, so the reader must never lag the writer.

entries.title: hasOppositePolarity matches on word-boundary regexes, not substrings
entries.summary: audn.ts hasOppositePolarity tests NEGATIVE_PATTERNS/POSITIVE_PATTERNS with precompiled word-boundary regexes, so "prefixed" no longer collides with "fixed".

entries.title: fleet-sprint primes the KB per member, never against the server cwd
entries.summary: The fleet-sprint engine has no repo path of its own -- it coordinates members by name and branch, and the repo lives on each member side. So each member work folder is resolved via member_detail and primed individually, and a member whose folder cannot be resolved is SKIPPED rather than primed blind, because kb_session_prime without repo_path reads whichever repo the fleet server sits in.

entries.title: resolveRepoPath shares one precedence rule across the KB tools
entries.summary: kb_export, kb_import and kb_session_prime each resolve a repo path as: explicit input, else the validated process working directory, else refuse. Every tier is validated with existsSync + isDirectory before use; there is no bare cwd fallback.

entries.title: Agent contracts need ToolSearch in frontmatter or their KB step is dead prose
entries.summary: Every role Step 0 Knowledge Bank block opens by loading the MCP KB tools through ToolSearch. A role whose frontmatter tools list omits ToolSearch cannot run that block, so the contract satisfies a grep for kb_ while priming nothing. The four roles that lacked a Step 0 were exactly the four without ToolSearch.

entries.title: An entry with no source_files can never be staled by the freshness sweep
entries.summary: freshnessSweep() builds its work set only from entries with a parsed source_file_hashes basis, so an entry citing no files is never checked and never staled -- permanently CONFIRMED-able and structurally unfalsifiable. This is the reason capture now refuses such entries.

entries.title: kb_export emits only live CONFIRMED entries
entries.summary: kbExport calls provider.list({confidence:"CONFIRMED"}) and list() hard-filters superseded_at IS NULL AND stale=0, so any entry that ends UNVERIFIED/INFERRED or stale=1 is silently absent from the bible.

entries.title: The HTTP capture route can reach only one capture() argument
entries.summary: The /api/kb/capture route calls provider.capture(JSON.parse(body)) with exactly one argument, so capture()'s second opts parameter -- importMode, preferredId -- is structurally unreachable from any deserialized route body.

entries.title: Capture fails closed on an uncheckable basis, at the provider choke point
entries.summary: SqliteProvider.capture() rejects an entry with zero source_files, and one citing files absent from the repo, throwing KbCaptureRejected. There is no exemption for source=harvest or for importMode; only user-directive is exempt from the empty-basis half, because a standing instruction is not a claim about code. Enforcement is in the provider because three of the four capture call sites -- kb_harvest, kb_import and the HTTP route -- never touch the kb_capture handler.

entries.title: kb_promote requires recorded evidence and a basis that still resolves
entries.summary: promote() is the only path that mints CONFIRMED, so it refuses a reason shorter than 20 characters and refuses an entry whose source_files no longer resolve (zero source_files included, since rows predating the capture gate still exist). capture() and promote() share one unresolvableBasisFiles() helper so an entry that was legitimately capturable can never be un-promotable.

entries.title: An export whose entry set is unchanged must rewrite nothing
entries.summary: Auto-committing the bible moves HEAD, so re-reading HEAD on the next export recorded a different provenance.commit, rewrote the file and committed again -- an export that never converges. entriesUnchanged() compares the entries only, never the provenance envelope, which also keeps the recorded commit honest: it names the tree the entries were verified against, not the commit that stored them.

entries.title: The confidence clamp is enforced in SqliteProvider.capture, not the tool handler
entries.summary: A non-directive CONFIRMED capture is downgraded to INFERRED with a bracketed note inside SqliteProvider.capture(), so the HTTP /api/kb/capture route cannot mint CONFIRMED by bypassing the kb_capture handler. kb_promote is the only path that mints CONFIRMED.
